textbookBox.concept: A compass has a fixed point that stays on the paper and a pencil end that moves. We open it against a ruler to set the distance between the two tips, and then turn it to draw a curve.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Many pictures are built from circles and parts of circles, called arcs. A wavy line along a central line AB of 8 cm can be drawn as half circles.

textbookBox.concept: In a rectangle ABCD, A, B, C and D are the corners, AB, BC, CD and DA are the sides, and the angles are angle A, B, C and D. AB and CD are a pair of opposite sides.

beats.en: In a rectangle ABCD, A, B, C and D are the corners, AB, BC, CD and DA are the sides, and the angles are angle A, B, C and D. AB and CD are a pair of opposite sides.
beats.speakEn: In a rectangle ABCD, A, B, C and D are the corners, AB, BC, CD and DA are the sides, and the angles are angle A, B, C and D. AB and CD are a pair of opposite sides.

beats.en: To construct a rectangle with sides of 5 cm and 3 cm, draw the side DC of 5 cm. At D and C construct lines perpendicular to DC, making 90 degree angles. Open the compass to 3 cm.
beats.speakEn: To construct a rectangle with sides of 5 centimetres and 3 centimetres, draw the side DC of 5 centimetres. At D and C construct lines perpendicular to DC, making 90 degree angles. Open the compass to 3 centimetres.

type: In a rectangle ABCD, A, B, C and D are the corners, AB, BC, CD and DA are the sides, and the angles
